title: Early–Middle Holocene humid period in the central Mediterranean from speleothem growth at Grotta della Serratura (Southern Italy)
content:
ABSTRACT

A phase of speleothem deposition within the Holocene archeological succession of the Serratura Cave (Southern Italy) indicates a period of increasing precipitation in the area. The related increment of cave dripping was probably responsible for the cessation of human occupation in the cave, because of unfavorable conditions. 230Th/U dating of one flowstone and three stalagmites indicate carbonate deposition from ca. 9.5 to 7.8 ka BP. This interval of growth is in reasonable agreement with a wetter phase identified by δ18O record at Corchia Cave and increasing flooding at Renella Cave, both in the Apuan Alps (Central Italy). A review of terrestrial records in peninsular Italy further evidences a wetter Early–Middle Holocene, although lacustrine lake level may suggest different seasonal distribution of rainfall in different areas. However, there are still several open questions concerning the chronology of this wetter interval and its synchronicity over different areas.
